title: Her mother's early death and grandmother's death
summary: Mother died when she was months old; grandmother died at 91; heart deaths in the family and an uncle's fatal fall.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Do you remember your mother much? Oh, no. No, my mother died. I was just about two months, I think. I was two or three months old. Well, I thought you were just a baby.
I didn't— Yeah, I was a baby. No, I don't remember at all.
And your grandmother, how long did she live?
Until I was 27 years old. 27? Yes.
So, where was she by when she died?

She was 91, I think. 91, wasn't she? Yes, uh-huh. But strong and healthy. She had asthma all of her life, and she weakened her heart. And she was coming through the door one day, and she told her daughter, I need some cool water. And when she came back, my grandmother had slumped. And I think she lived three weeks after that. Yeah. But they were doing everything they could for her. My sister came out in heart condition, honest. Honest, because everybody in my family died in heart. My aunt and her two sons died. I mean, just overnight. Just dropped—I mean, not sick at all. Just dropped dead. And my uncle, he was 87 when he died. That was the—Henry? Henry Mornad. Mornad, yes. And he fell out of a—slipped out of a bathtub and hit his head. And he never did get over the shark. Not at that age.

No. And you see, my cousins had taken him out of his home to their home. And he wasn't used to that little bathtub without that ring on the side. Well, you can catch on. She's a new bathtub you can't catch on.
